title: 桥洞下的自行车修理铺
title_en: Under the Railway Bridge: A Bike Mechanic on What We Get Wrong
summary_zh: 一位从音乐老师转行的自行车修理师，聊她怎么入行、大家保养自行车最常犯的错，以及这份工作最让她开心的瞬间。读完你能学会谈论转行和给出实用建议的表达。
body: Q: How did you end up running a bike repair shop? Hannah: Completely by accident. I was a music teacher, and I used to fix my friends' bikes at weekends. One day I realised I was looking forward to Saturday far more than Monday, so I rented this tiny space under the railway bridge. Q: What do people get wrong about looking after a bike? Hannah: Most people only think about their bike when it stops working. They ride it through rain and mud for months, and then they're surprised when the chain sounds like a box of spoons. Q: So what's the one thing everyone should do? Hannah: Keep the tyres pumped up. If your tyres are soft, every journey feels like riding uphill, and you're far more likely to get a puncture. Q: And the chain? Hannah: Wipe it with an old cloth to get the dirt off, then oil it lightly. Whenever someone brings in a chain that's dripping with oil, I know they've been trying too hard, because too much oil just collects dirt. Q: Do you ever turn a job down? Hannah: Not really, but sometimes I tell people honestly that fixing an old bike will cost more than it's worth. Even so, a lot of them want it repaired anyway, because the bike has a story. Q: What's the best part of the job? Hannah: When a kid comes back after a week and says the bike feels brand new. Although I've done this for years, that never gets old. Q: Any last advice? Hannah: Learn to fix a puncture yourself. One day, miles from home, you'll be glad you did.

questions.prompt: What does Hannah suggest about the way most people treat their bikes?
options: They spend too much money on expensive new parts
They only pay attention to the bike once something goes wrong
They clean their bikes far more often than necessary
They avoid riding in bad weather to protect the bike
questions.evidence: Most people only think about their bike when it stops working.

questions.prompt: Why does a chain dripping with oil show that someone has been "trying too hard"?
options: Extra oil makes the chain more likely to break
Extra oil is expensive and quickly runs out
Too much oil makes the chain collect more dirt
Too much oil makes the bike harder to pedal uphill
questions.evidence: because too much oil just collects dirt

questions.prompt: What is the interview mainly about?
options: A bike mechanic's simple advice on looking after a bike
Why old bikes should be thrown away
How to become a music teacher
The history of a railway bridge
questions.evidence: So what's the one thing everyone should do?

questions.prompt: What does "puncture" mean in "you're far more likely to get a puncture"?
options: a parking fine
a steep road
a small hole in a tyre
a broken chain
questions.evidence: you're far more likely to get a puncture

vocabulary.meaning: 轮胎（英式拼写，美式为 tires）
vocabulary.example: Check your tyres before a long ride.
I had to walk home because my front wheel got a puncture.
Riding uphill with a heavy bag is exhausting.
He came in from the rain with his coat dripping.
Lightly brush the bread with oil before you toast it.

expressions.note: end up + doing 表示“最终落得/走到……”，强调结果出乎意料：I ended up staying for a week.
回答“你怎么开始做这个的”时很常用，带点轻松自嘲。
to 是介词，后面接名词或动名词：I'm looking forward to seeing you.

expressions.meaning: 花的钱比它本身还值钱；不划算
expressions.note: 评价修理、维护是否值得时常用：Repairing that phone would cost more than it's worth.
形容一件事无论经历多少次都让人开心，非常口语。

expressions.meaning: 你会庆幸自己这么做了
expressions.note: 给建议时的收尾句，语气友好又有说服力。

knowledge.quote: If your tyres are soft, every journey feels like riding uphill, and you're far more likely to get a puncture.
knowledge.explanation: if + 一般现在时，主句也用一般现在时，描述“只要条件成立就会出现”的普遍结果，适合讲经验和规律。

knowledge.quote: Although I've done this for years, that never gets old.
knowledge.explanation: although 引导让步状语从句：前面说“做了很多年”，后面却说“从不腻”，形成对比。注意 although 和 but 不能在同一句里同时用。

knowledge.quote: Wipe it with an old cloth to get the dirt off, then oil it lightly.
knowledge.explanation: to get the dirt off 是不定式表目的，说明“为什么要擦”；给步骤说明时，动作 + to do 是最简洁的写法。

speaking: 用 1 分钟介绍一件你会修、会保养的东西（自行车、电脑、植物等），给听众一个最重要的建议，用上 If ..., ... 和 you'll be glad you did。
writing: 用 150–180 词写一段采访稿，采访一位你认识的手艺人或店主，至少包含三个问题，并在回答中用上 end up doing 和 although。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 One day I realised I was ...ing ... far more than ..., so I ... 讲一次让你改变方向的小顿悟。
task.model: One day I realised I was looking forward to Saturday far more than Monday, so I rented this tiny space under the railway bridge.

title: 合租分摊费用，怎么谈才不伤和气
title_en: Splitting the Bills Without Splitting the Flat
summary_zh: 合租矛盾往往不在钱多钱少，而在“有人觉得不公平却没人说”。这篇指南教你提前谈、说清什么算共用、定期回顾，用沟通代替憋气。
body: Money is one of the quickest ways to turn friendly flatmates into polite strangers. The problem is rarely the amount itself; it is the feeling that someone is getting a better deal and nobody is saying so. Fortunately, most of these tensions can be avoided with a few honest conversations. Start before the first bill arrives. Although it can feel awkward to talk about money with people you barely know, it is far easier to agree on rules early than to argue about them later. Next, decide together what counts as shared. Washing-up liquid and toilet paper are obvious, but what about olive oil, or a film subscription that only one person watches? Then be open about situations that are genuinely different. If one person works from home all day, they will probably use more heating, and it is fairer to say so out loud than to hint at it. Splitting everything equally is simple, but simple is not always the same as fair. Whatever system you choose, write it down somewhere everyone can see it, so that nobody has to rely on memory. Finally, agree to check in every few months, because routines change and a system that worked in autumn may feel unfair by summer. The aim is not to count every last coin but to make sure nobody quietly feels taken advantage of. When flatmates can talk about money as calmly as they talk about whose turn it is to take the bins out, the subject loses most of its power to spoil a home.

questions.prompt: According to the guide, what usually causes money arguments between flatmates?
options: Bills that are simply too high for anyone to pay
A sense of unfairness that nobody talks about openly
Flatmates who refuse to pay for anything at all
Disagreements about which shops to buy things from
questions.evidence: it is the feeling that someone is getting a better deal and nobody is saying so

questions.prompt: What does the writer suggest about splitting everything equally?
options: It is the only fair system for people sharing a flat
It should be avoided because it always causes arguments
It is easy, but it may not suit everyone's situation
It only works if everyone works from home
questions.evidence: Splitting everything equally is simple, but simple is not always the same as fair.

questions.prompt: Why does the writer compare talking about money with talking about taking the bins out?
options: Money should become an ordinary, calm topic in the flat
Money and rubbish both cause mess
Bills should be kept near the bins
Flatmates argue most about the bins
questions.evidence: the subject loses most of its power to spoil a home

questions.prompt: What does "taken advantage of" mean in "nobody quietly feels taken advantage of"?
options: given a reward
treated unfairly so that others benefit
left alone
asked for advice
questions.evidence: nobody quietly feels taken advantage of

vocabulary.example: There were tensions in the team after the meeting.
There was an awkward silence after he told the joke.
I cancelled my music subscription because I never used it.

vocabulary.meaning: 日常安排；作息习惯（复数）
vocabulary.example: Our routines changed completely when the baby was born.
Don't let one rude comment spoil your whole day.

expressions.meaning: 占了便宜；得到更划算的待遇
expressions.note: a better deal 不只指买东西，也可以指分工、待遇上的“更划算”。
用来界定范围：What counts as a shared item?
say so = 这样说；out loud 强调“说出口”，常和 hint（暗示）对比。
hint at + 事情，指不直说而是暗示，常带点消极意味。
除了酒店入住，也指和人定期聊聊进展：Let's check in next week.
feel taken advantage of 描述“觉得自己吃亏、被利用”，是合租、工作里很实用的说法。

knowledge.quote: Although it can feel awkward to talk about money with people you barely know, it is far easier to agree on rules early than to argue about them later.
knowledge.explanation: although 引导让步状语从句，先承认“确实尴尬”，再给出主句的建议，是说服别人时先退一步再推进的常用结构。

knowledge.quote: If one person works from home all day, they will probably use more heating
knowledge.explanation: if + 一般现在时，主句 will + 动词原形，描述现实中很可能出现的情况；加 probably 让判断不那么绝对。

knowledge.quote: The aim is not to count every last coin but to make sure nobody quietly feels taken advantage of.
knowledge.explanation: 两个不定式 to count / to make sure 作表语，说明 the aim 是什么；not to A but to B 用来澄清真正的目标。

speaking: 用 1 分钟给即将合租的朋友提建议：哪些东西应该一起分摊、哪些不该，以及怎样提出“不公平”而不伤感情，用上 what counts as 和 check in。
writing: 用 150–180 词写一份合租“共用物品约定”的说明，解释为什么这样分配，至少用一次 although 和一次 not to ... but to ...。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 The aim is not to ... but to ... 说明你做某件事的真正目的。
task.model: The aim is not to count every last coin but to make sure nobody quietly feels taken advantage of.

title: 帮邻居看猫，差点全楼出动
title_en: The Weekend I Became the Building's Cat Detective
summary_zh: “我”答应帮邻居照看猫，却没读她留的纸条，以为猫跑丢了，发动全楼去找。读完你能学会讲一个“反转”小故事，并掌握错综时间条件句。
body: When my neighbour Helen asked me to feed her cat for a weekend, I agreed without thinking twice. How hard could it be? She handed me a key, a bag of food and a note written in tiny handwriting, which I folded into my pocket without reading. On Saturday morning, I let myself in, filled the bowl and called the cat's name. Nothing happened. I checked under the bed, behind the curtains and inside every cupboard, but Mango was nowhere to be found. Because a window in the kitchen was slightly open, I convinced myself that she had escaped. For the next three hours, I knocked on every door in the building, shook a box of cat treats in the car park and even printed posters with a photo borrowed from Helen's fridge door. By the afternoon, half of my neighbours were searching the street with me. It was only when I went back to the flat to leave some food out that I finally unfolded the note. On the second side, underlined twice, Helen had explained that Mango hides on top of the wardrobe whenever strangers visit, and that I shouldn't worry if I never saw her. I opened the bedroom door, looked up, and there she was, staring down at me with complete calm. Had I turned that note over on the first morning, I wouldn't now be known to everyone in our building as the cat detective. Helen laughed for a full minute when she got home, but she has already asked me to look after Mango again next month. This time, I have read the instructions twice.

questions.prompt: What was the real cause of the narrator's problem?
options: Helen forgot to explain where the cat liked to hide
The cat really did escape through the kitchen window
The narrator didn't read the instructions they had been given
The neighbours frightened the cat by searching too loudly
questions.evidence: which I folded into my pocket without reading

questions.prompt: Why did the narrator believe the cat had escaped?
options: The front door had been left unlocked
A kitchen window was a little open
A neighbour had seen a cat in the car park
The food in the bowl had not been touched
questions.evidence: Because a window in the kitchen was slightly open, I convinced myself that she had escaped.

questions.prompt: Why has Helen asked the narrator to look after Mango again?
options: She found the mix-up funny and still trusts the narrator
The narrator offered to pay her
Mango now prefers the narrator
Nobody else in the building will do it
questions.evidence: Helen laughed for a full minute when she got home, but she has already asked me to look after Mango again next month.

questions.prompt: What does "convinced myself" mean in "I convinced myself that she had escaped"?
options: made myself believe something
proved something with evidence
forgot completely
told a neighbour
questions.evidence: I convinced myself that she had escaped

vocabulary.example: I can't read the doctor's handwriting on this note.
She convinced me to try the spicy soup.
Our rabbit escaped from the garden last night.
The teacher underlined the most important words in red.
The baby kept staring at the balloons.

expressions.note: 形容答应得很爽快，常暗示后面会出问题。
带反讽的自问，讲故事时常用来预示“其实很难”。
let oneself in 指主人不在时自己进门，帮人看家时很常用。
比 I couldn't find it 更有画面感和戏剧性。
convince oneself that ... 常指在没有证据的情况下认定某事。
there + 代词 + was 表示“终于看到”，讲故事时制造揭晓的瞬间。

knowledge.quote: Had I turned that note over on the first morning, I wouldn't now be known to everyone in our building as the cat detective.
knowledge.explanation: 条件说的是过去（当时没翻看纸条），结果说的是现在（如今被全楼叫作“猫侦探”），所以前半句用 had done，后半句用 would (not) now be。Had I turned = If I had turned，倒装更书面。

knowledge.quote: Because a window in the kitchen was slightly open, I convinced myself that she had escaped.
knowledge.explanation: because 引导原因状语从句放在句首，先给出“误导性的线索”，再说结论，讲故事时能制造悬念。

knowledge.quote: It was only when I went back to the flat to leave some food out that I finally unfolded the note.
knowledge.explanation: to leave some food out 是不定式表目的，说明回去的原因；整句还用了 It was only when ... that ... 强调句，突出“直到那时才……”。

speaking: 用 1 分钟讲一次你因为没看说明、没听清话而闹出的误会，最后用一句 Had I ..., I wouldn't now ... 总结。
writing: 用 150–180 词写一个帮别人照看东西（宠物、植物、房子）时出了小意外的故事，用上 nowhere to be found 和 there it was。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 Had I ..., I wouldn't now ... 写一句因为过去一个小疏忽而导致现在某种结果的话。
task.model: Had I turned that note over on the first morning, I wouldn't now be known to everyone in our building as the cat detective.

title: 城市中心该不该禁止汽车
title_en: Should Cities Ban Cars from Their Centres?
summary_zh: 一篇考试风格的议论文：作者支持市中心禁行私家车，但认为必须循序渐进、照顾商户和行动不便者。读完你能学会“立论—让步—反驳—结论”的写法。
body: Few questions divide a city as quickly as what to do about cars in its centre. In my view, most cities would benefit from closing their central streets to private cars, provided that the change is made gradually and with real alternatives in place. The case for a ban is easy to picture. Without traffic, a busy junction can become a square where children play and neighbours stop to chat. The air is cleaner, the noise drops, and walking or cycling no longer feels like a risk. If a centre is pleasant to spend time in, people tend to stay longer, which can be good news for cafés and small shops. Critics, however, raise serious concerns. Shop owners worry that customers who drive in from the suburbs will simply go elsewhere. Older people and those with limited mobility may depend on a car to reach the places they need. Delivery drivers and emergency services also need access. Although these objections are sometimes dismissed as excuses, they describe real lives. Yet they are an argument for a careful ban rather than no ban at all. A sensible plan would allow deliveries at certain hours, keep access for people who genuinely need it, and improve buses before the first street is closed. It is also worth remembering that many old city centres were laid out long before the car existed and were only later reshaped around it. If planners had resisted that change, we would not be having this argument today. Handled with care, a car-free centre is not a loss but a return to what those streets were built for.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's overall position?
options: Cars should be banned from every city centre immediately
City centres should be closed to private cars, but carefully and step by step
Cars are essential in city centres, so a ban would be a mistake
Shop owners should be the ones to decide whether cars are allowed
questions.evidence: provided that the change is made gradually and with real alternatives in place

questions.prompt: How does the writer respond to the critics' concerns?
options: By saying the concerns are only excuses to avoid change
By admitting that the concerns make a ban impossible
By arguing that the concerns show how a ban should be designed
By suggesting that critics should move out of the city centre
questions.evidence: they are an argument for a careful ban rather than no ban at all

questions.prompt: What does the writer mean by "a return to what those streets were built for"?
options: Cars should be allowed back into the centre
Old centres were designed for people on foot, before cars existed
Cities should rebuild their old walls
Streets were first built for buses
questions.evidence: many old city centres were laid out long before the car existed

questions.prompt: What does "limited mobility" mean in "those with limited mobility"?
options: a small budget
poor eyesight
a short holiday
difficulty in moving around easily

vocabulary.example: Turn left at the next junction.
The new lift helps people with limited mobility reach the platform.
Several neighbours raised objections to the new car park.

vocabulary.meaning: 不予理会；（把……）当作不重要而否定
vocabulary.example: His idea was dismissed before he could explain it properly.
Taking an umbrella would be the sensible thing to do.

expressions.note: 议论文亮明立场的标准开头，比 I think 更正式。

expressions.meaning: 在有了真正替代方案的前提下
expressions.note: in place 表示“已经到位、准备好”：Make sure the new system is in place first.
the case for/against + 名词，议论文里用来引出正方或反方论据。
常用来说顾客流失：If prices go up, customers will go elsewhere.

expressions.text: rather than no ban at all
expressions.note: A rather than B 用来在两种选择中表明立场，反驳时很有力。
议论文中引入一个容易被忽略的背景或事实，语气克制。

knowledge.quote: If a centre is pleasant to spend time in, people tend to stay longer
knowledge.explanation: if + 一般现在时，主句一般现在时（tend to），表达一种普遍规律，适合在议论文里陈述论据。

knowledge.quote: Although these objections are sometimes dismissed as excuses, they describe real lives.
knowledge.explanation: although 引导让步状语从句，先承认对方观点常被轻视，再强调它的价值，是议论文“让步”段的典型句式。

knowledge.quote: If planners had resisted that change, we would not be having this argument today.
knowledge.explanation: 条件指过去（当年规划者没有抵制），结果指现在（今天才会有这场争论），所以前半句用 had done，后半句用 would be doing + today。

speaking: 用 1 分钟说说你所在城市的市中心是否应该限制汽车，先说观点，再承认一个反对理由，最后回应它，用上 In my view 和 rather than。
writing: 写一篇 200–250 词的议论文，题目自拟（如“城市是否应该增加自行车道”），包含明确论点、一个让步段和结论，至少用一次 Although ... 和一次错综条件句。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 ... are an argument for A rather than no A at all 回应一个反对意见，说明它只说明“要谨慎”，而不是“别做”。
task.model: they are an argument for a careful ban rather than no ban at all
